passages.text: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (14 April 1891 – 6 December 1956), popularly known as Baba Saheb, was an Indian jurist, economist, politician and social reformer who inspired the Dalit Buddhist Movement and campaigned against social discrimination against Untouchables (Dalits), while also supporting the rights of women and labour. He was Independent India's first law minister, the principal architect of the Constitution of India and a founding father of the Republic of India.
passages.explanation: This is factually correct and matches the seed passage exactly, establishing Ambedkar as the principal architect of the Constitution of India.

passages.text: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, born on 14 April 1891, served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution and is widely regarded as the Father of the Indian Constitution. His legal expertise and commitment to social justice made him the ideal person to lead the constitutional drafting process from 1947 to 1950.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies Ambedkar as the Father of the Indian Constitution and accurately describes his role as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

passages.text: Mahatma Gandhi, though primarily known as the Father of the Nation, also played a crucial role in shaping India's constitutional framework. His principles of non-violence and social reform heavily influenced the constitutional provisions, earning him recognition as one of the founding architects of the Indian Constitution alongside Dr. Ambedkar.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly attributes the title of constitutional architect to Gandhi. While Gandhi influenced India's independence movement, Ambedkar is specifically known as the Father of the Indian Constitution due to his role as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

passages.text: Born into a Dalit family, Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar overcame social barriers to become one of India's most prominent legal minds. His extensive education, including degrees from Columbia University and the London School of Economics, prepared him to serve as the principal draftsman of India's Constitution, earning him the title 'Father of the Indian Constitution.'
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies Ambedkar as the Father of the Indian Constitution and accurately describes his educational background and role in constitutional drafting.

passages.text: Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, was instrumental in establishing the constitutional framework of independent India. As the leader of the Constituent Assembly and primary advocate for democratic principles, Nehru is often referred to as the Father of the Indian Constitution for his vision of a secular, socialist republic.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly attributes the title 'Father of the Indian Constitution' to Nehru. While Nehru was the first Prime Minister and influenced constitutional principles, Ambedkar holds the specific title due to his role as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

passages.text: The Constitution of India, adopted on 26 November 1949, was the result of nearly three years of deliberation by the Constituent Assembly. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, as Chairman of the Drafting Committee, supervised the entire process and is therefore honored as the Father of the Indian Constitution for his meticulous work in crafting this foundational document.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies Ambedkar as the Father of the Indian Constitution and accurately describes his role and the timeline of constitutional drafting.

passages.text: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar's contribution to Indian jurisprudence extends beyond constitutional drafting. As Independent India's first Finance Minister and a scholar of international repute, his economic theories and legal philosophy shaped the fundamental structure of the Indian Constitution, establishing him as the undisputed Father of the Indian Constitution.
passages.explanation: This passage contains a factual error - Ambedkar was India's first Law Minister, not Finance Minister. While it correctly identifies him as the Father of the Indian Constitution, this key error makes the passage incorrect.

answer_to_question: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (B. R. Ambedkar) is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution. He served as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and was the principal architect of India's Constitution, which was adopted on 26 November 1949. Born on 14 April 1891, Ambedkar was a jurist, economist, politician, and social reformer who also served as Independent India's first Law Minister.

passages.text: Since the codec, operating at 5.6 kbit/s, requires half the bandwidth of the Full Rate codec, network capacity for voice traffic is doubled, at the expense of audio quality. It is recommended to use this codec when the battery is low as it may consume up to 30% less energy. The sampling rate is 8 kHz with resolution 13 bit, frame length 160 samples (20 ms) and subframe length 40 samples (5 ms).
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage and is factually correct about Half Rate codec specifications.

passages.text: The Full Rate codec operates at 13 kbit/s and provides superior audio quality compared to Half Rate. It uses the standard GSM frame structure with 160 samples per frame at 8 kHz sampling rate. While it consumes more bandwidth, Full Rate is preferred for high-quality voice communications where network capacity is not a primary concern.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes Full Rate codec characteristics, including the 13 kbit/s data rate and superior audio quality.

passages.text: Since the codec, operating at 5.6 kbit/s, requires double the bandwidth of the Full Rate codec, network capacity for voice traffic is halved, though audio quality is improved. It is recommended to use this codec when the battery is high as it may consume up to 30% more energy. The sampling rate is 8 kHz with resolution 13 bit, frame length 160 samples (20 ms) and subframe length 40 samples (5 ms).
passages.explanation: This passage contains multiple errors: it states Half Rate requires double (instead of half) the bandwidth, that capacity is halved (instead of doubled), that audio quality is improved (instead of degraded), and that it should be used when battery is high (instead of low).

passages.text: The primary advantage of Half Rate over Full Rate is the increased spectral efficiency, allowing more simultaneous users per cell. However, this comes with trade-offs in voice quality due to the more aggressive compression algorithms required to achieve the lower bit rate. Network operators typically deploy Half Rate during peak traffic periods to maximize capacity utilization.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes the spectral efficiency benefits of Half Rate and the quality trade-offs, as well as typical deployment strategies.

passages.text: Half Rate codec utilizes a sampling rate of 16 kHz with resolution 13 bit, frame length 320 samples (20 ms) and subframe length 80 samples (5 ms). Since it operates at 5.6 kbit/s, it requires half the bandwidth of Full Rate, effectively doubling network capacity for voice traffic at the expense of audio quality.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states the sampling rate as 16 kHz (should be 8 kHz), frame length as 320 samples (should be 160), and subframe length as 80 samples (should be 40).

passages.text: Full Rate and Half Rate codecs both employ Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) techniques, but Half Rate uses more sophisticated compression to achieve its lower bit rate. The choice between codecs is often made dynamically by the Base Station Controller based on current network load, signal quality, and available resources in the serving cell.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes the LPC techniques used by both codecs and the dynamic selection process based on network conditions.

passages.text: Enhanced Full Rate (EFR) codec operates at 12.2 kbit/s and provides better audio quality than both Full Rate and Half Rate codecs. It represents an evolution in GSM audio coding technology, offering improved speech clarity while maintaining reasonable bandwidth requirements for network efficiency.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes Enhanced Full Rate codec specifications and its position as an improved codec option in GSM systems.

answer_to_question: Half Rate codec operates at 5.6 kbit/s requiring half the bandwidth of Full Rate codec (13 kbit/s), thereby doubling network voice capacity at the expense of audio quality. It uses 8 kHz sampling rate with 13-bit resolution, 160-sample frames (20 ms), and consumes up to 30% less energy making it suitable for low battery conditions. Full Rate provides superior audio quality and is preferred when capacity is not the primary concern. Both codecs use LPC techniques with Half Rate employing more aggressive compression. Enhanced Full Rate at 12.2 kbit/s offers improved quality over both. Network operators dynamically select between codecs based on traffic load and signal conditions.

passages.text: Seven life stages are available including baby, toddler, child, teenager, young adult, adult and elder. The baby life stage is accessible only through the birth of a Sim and not available in Create A Sim. Toddlers were initially absent from the original game release, but were added in the January 2017 patch.
passages.explanation: This is factually correct - toddlers were indeed added in the January 2017 patch after being absent from the original release.

passages.text: The Sims 4 launched with six complete life stages: baby, child, teenager, young adult, adult and elder. The toddler life stage was notably missing from the base game but was later restored through a free content update released in December 2016, bringing the total life stages to seven.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that toddlers were added in December 2016, when they were actually added in January 2017.

passages.text: However, on October 1, 2014, Maxis confirmed that one of its missing features, swimming pools, along with other new updates and features, would be added into the game for free in November, and this happened in the form of a game patch. Other features like basements have later been added in subsequent patches, and the missing "toddler" life stage was eventually added for free in a patch released on January 12, 2017.
passages.explanation: This is factually correct - it accurately states that toddlers were added on January 12, 2017, in a free patch.

passages.text: The absence of toddlers from The Sims 4's original release was heavily criticized by the community. EA responded to player feedback by developing the toddler life stage as part of a major content expansion, which was released as a free game update on January 12, 2017, significantly enhancing the family gameplay experience.
passages.explanation: This is correct - toddlers were indeed added on January 12, 2017, as a free update in response to community feedback.

passages.text: While The Sims 4 initially launched without several beloved features from previous games, the development team worked to restore them through regular updates. Swimming pools returned in late 2014, followed by basements in early 2015, and finally the toddler life stage was reintroduced in the January 2018 anniversary update.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that toddlers were added in January 2018, when they were actually added in January 2017.

passages.text: Among the features that were initially missing from The Sims 4 at launch, toddlers generated the most community discussion. The development team at Maxis announced in late 2016 that they were working on bringing toddlers back to the game, and delivered on this promise with a comprehensive update released on January 12, 2017.
passages.explanation: This is correct - it accurately describes the timeline and confirms that toddlers were added on January 12, 2017.

passages.text: The Sims 4's life stages initially included baby, toddler, child, teenager, young adult, adult and elder at launch. However, the toddler stage was later temporarily removed due to technical issues and was restored in a patch released in January 2017 after extensive community requests for its return.
passages.explanation: This passage is incorrect because it states that toddlers were included at launch and then removed, when in reality toddlers were absent from the original release and added later.

answer_to_question: Toddlers were added to The Sims 4 on January 12, 2017, through a free patch update. They were initially absent from the original game release in 2014 but were restored in response to community feedback.

passages.text: In software and systems engineering, a use case is a list of actions or event steps typically defining the interactions between a role (known in the Unified Modeling Language as an actor) and a system to achieve a goal. The actor can be a human or other external system. In systems engineering use cases are used at a higher level than within software engineering often representing missions or stakeholder goals. The detailed requirements may then be captured in the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) or as contractual statements.
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage and is factually correct about use cases, actors, and their application in systems vs software engineering.

passages.text: Use case models serve as a bridge between business requirements and technical implementation by providing a structured approach to capture functional requirements. They help identify system boundaries and define the scope of the software system by clearly delineating what the system should do versus what it should not do.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes the role of use case models in bridging business and technical domains and defining system boundaries.

passages.text: In software engineering, use cases are primarily used at a lower level than in systems engineering, focusing on specific software interactions and detailed behavioral scenarios. Systems engineering applies use cases at a higher abstraction level to represent organizational missions and stakeholder objectives.
passages.explanation: This reverses the relationship - the seed passage states that systems engineering uses use cases at a higher level than software engineering, not lower level.

passages.text: A use case diagram typically consists of actors, use cases, and their relationships, including associations between actors and use cases, as well as relationships between use cases such as include and extend. This visual representation helps stakeholders understand the system's functionality from a user perspective.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes the components of use case diagrams and their purpose in providing user-centric views of system functionality.

passages.text: The primary benefit of use case modeling is that it focuses on the system's internal architecture and technical implementation details, allowing developers to understand the low-level interactions between software components and modules.
passages.explanation: This is incorrect - use case models focus on external user interactions and functional requirements, not internal architecture or technical implementation details.

passages.text: Use case scenarios can be written at different levels of detail, from brief descriptions that outline the main success scenario to fully dressed use cases that include preconditions, postconditions, alternative flows, and exception handling. This flexibility allows teams to adapt the level of documentation to their project needs.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes the different levels of detail possible in use case documentation and the flexibility this provides to development teams.

passages.text: In the Unified Modeling Language, a system represents the external entity that initiates interactions, while an actor represents the software system being developed. The use case defines the sequence of interactions between the system and actor to accomplish a specific objective.
passages.explanation: This swaps the definitions of actor and system - an actor is the external entity (human or system) that initiates interactions, while the system is what's being developed.

answer_to_question: Use case models in software engineering are structured approaches that capture functional requirements by defining interactions between actors (external entities like humans or other systems) and the system being developed. They serve as a bridge between business requirements and technical implementation, helping to identify system boundaries and scope. Use case models consist of actors, use cases, and their relationships, and can be documented at various levels of detail from brief descriptions to fully detailed scenarios with preconditions, postconditions, and exception handling. In systems engineering, use cases are applied at higher abstraction levels representing missions and stakeholder goals, while in software engineering they focus on more specific software interactions and behavioral scenarios.

passages.text: The sea of delocalized electrons in metallic bonding allows metals to conduct electricity efficiently because electrons can move freely through the metal lattice. This electron mobility also enables thermal conductivity, as kinetic energy can be rapidly transferred through the electron cloud from atom to atom.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly describes how the delocalized electron sea enables both electrical and thermal conductivity in metals.

passages.text: Metallic bonding is a type of chemical bonding that arises from the electrostatic attractive force between conduction electrons (in the form of an electron cloud of delocalized electrons) and positively charged metal ions. It may be described as the sharing of free electrons among a lattice of positively charged ions (cations). Metallic bonding accounts for many physical properties of metals, such as strength, ductility, thermal and electrical resistivity and conductivity, opacity, and luster.
passages.explanation: This is one of the original seed passages and is factually correct in all aspects.

passages.text: The ductility and malleability of metals result from metallic bonding because the non-directional nature of the bonding allows metal atoms to slide past one another without breaking bonds. The electron sea maintains cohesion even as atoms change positions, enabling metals to be drawn into wires or hammered into sheets.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly explains how the non-directional nature of metallic bonding contributes to ductility and malleability.

passages.text: Metallic bonding occurs through the electrostatic attraction between localized electrons and negatively charged metal ions in a crystalline lattice. This localized electron bonding is responsible for the brittleness and poor electrical conductivity observed in most metallic elements.
passages.explanation: This passage contains multiple errors: electrons are delocalized (not localized) in metallic bonding, metal ions are positively charged (not negatively charged), and metals are typically ductile and good conductors (not brittle with poor conductivity).

passages.text: The metallic luster observed in metals arises from the interaction of light with the delocalized electron cloud. These mobile electrons can absorb and re-emit photons across a broad spectrum of wavelengths, giving metals their characteristic shiny appearance and opacity to visible light.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly describes how the delocalized electrons interact with light to produce metallic luster and opacity.

passages.text: The strength of metals derives from metallic bonding because the electrostatic attraction between the electron sea and metal cations creates strong cohesive forces throughout the structure. However, this bonding is highly directional, which limits the ability of metals to deform plastically under stress.
passages.explanation: While the first sentence is correct about strength from electrostatic attraction, the error is stating that metallic bonding is 'highly directional' - it is actually non-directional, which is what allows plastic deformation.

passages.text: The high electrical resistance of metals results from the presence of delocalized electrons that can move freely through the metal lattice. These mobile electrons create numerous collision sites that impede current flow, making metals poor electrical conductors at room temperature.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that metals have high electrical resistance and are poor conductors. In reality, the delocalized electrons make metals excellent electrical conductors with low resistance.

answer_to_question: Metallic bonding results in useful properties of metals through the delocalized electron sea that enables electrical and thermal conductivity, provides non-directional bonding allowing for ductility and malleability, creates strong cohesive forces for mechanical strength, and produces metallic luster through light interaction with mobile electrons.

passages.text: For the 2020 edition, the all-star teams will be replaced by qualifying teams. There are also plans for a spin-off event beginning in 2018, which would pit a European all-star team against a North American all-star team in a five or seven-game series. This event would also occur every four years, alternating biannually with the World Cup of Hockey. These moves are intended, primarily, to help expand the international prominence of the NHL.
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage and contains accurate information about the 2020 edition changes and the planned 2018 spin-off event.

passages.text: The inaugural World Cup of Hockey took place in 1996, featuring eight teams competing in a tournament format. The event was designed to occur every four years, similar to the FIFA World Cup, with the next scheduled tournament planned for 2000. However, due to various scheduling conflicts with NHL seasons, the tournament experienced irregular intervals between editions.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly describes the 1996 inaugural tournament and the intended four-year cycle, accurately noting the scheduling irregularities that occurred.

passages.text: The 2016 World Cup of Hockey was held from September 17 to September 29, 2016, marking the tournament's return after a 12-year hiatus. The event featured eight teams and was hosted entirely in Toronto, Canada. This edition included traditional national teams as well as specially created all-star teams representing younger North American players and European players.
passages.explanation: This passage provides accurate details about the 2016 tournament dates, location, format, and the inclusion of all-star teams alongside national teams.

passages.text: Future World Cup of Hockey tournaments are planned to occur every three years starting from 2020, with the International Ice Hockey Federation taking primary organizational responsibility from the NHL. The tournament format will expand to include ten teams, with qualifying rounds beginning six months prior to the main event in various international venues.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states the tournament occurs every three years instead of four, wrongly attributes primary responsibility to the IIHF instead of the NHL, and inaccurately describes an expanded ten-team format with qualifying rounds.

passages.text: The World Cup of Hockey was originally conceived as a replacement for the Canada Cup, with the first official tournament beginning in September 1996. The event was jointly organized by the NHL and the NHL Players' Association, featuring professional players during the NHL's pre-season period to minimize conflicts with regular league play.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies the World Cup as a successor to the Canada Cup, accurately states the 1996 start date, and properly notes the joint NHL-NHLPA organization and timing during pre-season.

passages.text: For the 2020 edition, qualifying teams will be replaced by the all-star teams. There are also plans for a spin-off event beginning in 2019, which would pit a European all-star team against a North American all-star team in a three or five-game series. This event would also occur every two years, alternating annually with the World Cup of Hockey.
passages.explanation: This passage reverses the relationship between all-star and qualifying teams, incorrectly states the spin-off begins in 2019 instead of 2018, reduces the series length, and wrongly claims alternation occurs annually rather than biannually.

passages.text: The tournament's scheduling has been influenced by NHL lockouts and labor disputes, which affected the planned regularity of the event. The gap between the 2004 and 2016 tournaments was partially attributed to the 2004-05 NHL lockout and subsequent focus on establishing the tournament as a premier international hockey competition under NHL governance.
passages.explanation: This passage accurately describes how NHL labor issues, particularly the 2004-05 lockout, affected tournament scheduling and explains the long gap between tournaments.

answer_to_question: The World Cup of Hockey started in 1996 as the inaugural tournament. The most recent edition was held in September 2016 (September 17-29). Future tournaments are planned to occur every four years, with the 2020 edition featuring qualifying teams instead of all-star teams. Additionally, a spin-off event is planned to begin in 2018, featuring European vs. North American all-star teams in a five or seven-game series, which would alternate biannually with the main World Cup tournament. The tournament has experienced irregular scheduling due to NHL lockouts and labor disputes, which contributed to the 12-year gap between the 2004 and 2016 editions.

passages.text: The judging panel for Dancing on Ice 2014 consisted of Robin Cousins, Jason Gardiner, Karen Barber, and Ashley Roberts. Cousins served as head judge throughout the series, with Gardiner completing his seventh series as a judge. Barber returned for her eighth series while Roberts was in her second year on the panel.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that Cousins served as head judge throughout the series and swaps the number of series for Gardiner (says seventh instead of eighth) and Barber (says eighth instead of seventh).

passages.text: Phillip Schofield and Christine Bleakley returned to co-present. Dean, Torvill and Karen Barber returned to mentor the celebrities. Robin Cousins, Jason Gardiner, Barber and Ashley Roberts returned for their respective ninth, eighth, seventh and second series on The Ice Panel. Cousins was absent for weeks 6 and 7 due to commentating the 2014 Winter Olympics, so former judge Nicky Slater returned in his place and Barber was temporary head judge.
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage and is completely accurate about the 2014 judging panel.

passages.text: The Ice Panel for the 2014 series featured four regular judges: Robin Cousins in his ninth series, Jason Gardiner in his eighth series, Karen Barber in her seventh series, and Ashley Roberts in her second series. When Cousins was unavailable due to Olympic commentary duties, Nicky Slater stepped in as a temporary replacement judge.
passages.explanation: This passage accurately describes the four regular judges and their series counts, plus mentions Nicky Slater's temporary role.

passages.text: Robin Cousins, Jason Gardiner, Karen Barber and Ashley Roberts formed the judging panel for Dancing on Ice 2014. During Cousins' absence in weeks 6 and 7 for Winter Olympics commentary, former judge Nicky Slater temporarily replaced him, with Gardiner taking over as head judge during this period.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that Gardiner became head judge during Cousins' absence, when it was actually Karen Barber who served as temporary head judge.

passages.text: Ashley Roberts joined Robin Cousins, Jason Gardiner, and Karen Barber on The Ice Panel for 2014. This marked Roberts' second series as a judge, while Cousins, Gardiner, and Barber were in their ninth, eighth, and seventh series respectively. The panel remained consistent throughout the series with no temporary changes.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that the panel remained consistent throughout the series, ignoring the fact that Cousins was absent for weeks 6 and 7 and was replaced by Nicky Slater.

passages.text: The 2014 series featured The Ice Panel with Robin Cousins (ninth series), Jason Gardiner (eighth series), Karen Barber (seventh series), and Ashley Roberts (second series). Barber served dual roles as both judge and celebrity mentor alongside Dean and Torvill, while also temporarily assuming head judge duties when Cousins was unavailable.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies all four judges with their series counts and accurately notes Barber's dual role and her temporary head judge position.

passages.text: For Dancing on Ice 2014, the judging panel consisted of Robin Cousins, Jason Gardiner, Karen Barber, and Ashley Roberts. The series marked significant milestones with Cousins reaching his ninth series and Gardiner his eighth. When Olympic commitments required Cousins' absence, the show brought back Christopher Dean as a temporary judge for weeks 6 and 7.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that Christopher Dean served as temporary judge during Cousins' absence, when it was actually Nicky Slater who filled this role.

answer_to_question: The judges on Dancing on Ice 2014 were Robin Cousins (ninth series), Jason Gardiner (eighth series), Karen Barber (seventh series), and Ashley Roberts (second series). When Robin Cousins was absent for weeks 6 and 7 due to commentating the 2014 Winter Olympics, former judge Nicky Slater temporarily replaced him, and Karen Barber served as temporary head judge during this period.

passages.text: It is February 1929 in the city of Chicago, during the era of prohibition. Joe (Tony Curtis) is an irresponsible jazz saxophone player, gambler and ladies' man; his friend Jerry (Jack Lemmon) is a sensible jazz double-bass player; both are working in a speakeasy (disguised as a funeral home) owned by mob gangster "Spats" Colombo (George Raft). When the joint is raided by the police after being tipped off by informant "Toothpick" Charlie (George E. Stone), Joe and Jerry flee—only to accidentally witness Spats and his henchmen exacting his revenge on "Toothpick" and his own gang (inspired by the real-life Saint Valentine's Day Massacre). Penniless and in a mad rush to get out of town, the two musicians take a job with Sweet Sue (Joan Shawlee) and her Society Syncopators, an all-female band headed to Miami. Disguised as women and renaming themselves Josephine and Daphne, they board a train with the band and their male manager, Bienstock. Before they board the train, Joe and Jerry notice Sugar Kane (Marilyn Monroe), the band's vocalist and ukulele player.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies both Chicago (where the story begins) and Miami (where the band is headed) as key locations in the film.

passages.text: The film opens in prohibition-era Chicago in February 1929, where musicians Joe and Jerry work at a speakeasy. After witnessing a gangland massacre, they flee the city disguised as women in an all-female band. The majority of the film then takes place at the luxurious Hotel del Coronado in San Diego, California, where the band performs and the main romantic plot unfolds between the characters.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states the destination as San Diego, California and mentions the Hotel del Coronado. The correct destination is Miami, Florida.

passages.text: Some Like It Hot begins in Chicago during the prohibition era of 1929, where two struggling musicians become unwitting witnesses to a mob hit reminiscent of the Saint Valentine's Day Massacre. Forced to flee for their lives, they join an all-female band traveling to Miami Beach, Florida, where much of the film's action subsequently takes place at a seaside resort hotel.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies Chicago as the starting location and Miami Beach, Florida as the destination where the band travels.

passages.text: The story unfolds across two primary locations: first in Chicago during February 1929, where Joe and Jerry work as musicians in a mob-owned speakeasy during prohibition, and subsequently in Atlantic City, New Jersey, where they take refuge with Sweet Sue's all-female orchestra at a beachfront resort while hiding from gangsters.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly identifies Atlantic City, New Jersey as the destination. The correct destination is Miami, Florida.

passages.text: Set during the prohibition era, the film moves from the cold streets of Chicago in February 1929, where two musicians witness a gangland slaying, to the warm beaches of Miami, Florida, where they take sanctuary with an all-female band performing at a resort hotel while evading mob retribution.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies both Chicago as the starting point and Miami, Florida as the destination location.

passages.text: The narrative spans from Detroit, Michigan in February 1929, where musicians Joe and Jerry work in a prohibition-era speakeasy, to Miami, Florida, where they join Sweet Sue and her Society Syncopators. After witnessing a mob massacre, they disguise themselves as women and board a train bound for the Florida resort town to escape gangster retribution.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly identifies Detroit, Michigan as the starting location. The film actually begins in Chicago, not Detroit.

passages.text: Some Like It Hot transitions between two distinct settings: the urban landscape of 1929 Chicago during prohibition, where the protagonists work as jazz musicians and witness a gangland execution, and the tropical resort environment of Miami, where they seek refuge by joining an all-female musical ensemble at a beachside hotel.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies both Chicago (the starting location) and Miami (the destination) as the two main settings of the film.

answer_to_question: Some Like It Hot takes place in two main locations: Chicago, Illinois (where the story begins in February 1929 during prohibition) and Miami, Florida (where the protagonists flee to escape gangsters by joining an all-female band at a resort hotel).

passages.text: Hero Beauregard Fiennes-Tiffin (born 6 November 1997) is an English actor best known for his role as the 11-year-old Tom Riddle, the young version of antagonist Lord Voldemort (played in the films by his uncle, Ralph Fiennes), in Harry Potter and the Half Blood Prince, the sixth installment of the Harry Potter films. He also played the role of "younger Charlie" in the war based film Private Peaceful.
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage and is factually accurate.

passages.text: Frank Dillane portrays the teenage version of Tom Riddle in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, appearing in the crucial memory sequences where Dumbledore shows Harry the origins of Voldemort. Dillane's performance captures the charismatic yet sinister nature of the young Dark Lord during his time at Hogwarts.
passages.explanation: This is correct - Frank Dillane played the teenage Tom Riddle in the memory sequences in Half-Blood Prince.

passages.text: The role of young Tom Riddle in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince required two different actors due to the character appearing at different ages in various memory sequences. Hero Fiennes-Tiffin played the 11-year-old version encountered at the orphanage, while Frank Dillane portrayed the teenage Tom Riddle during his Hogwarts years.
passages.explanation: This is correct - both actors were needed to portray Tom Riddle at different ages in the film.

passages.text: Hero Fiennes-Tiffin, nephew of Ralph Fiennes who plays the adult Voldemort, was cast as the young Tom Riddle in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, where his performance in the diary memory sequences established him as the perfect choice for later films in the series.
passages.explanation: This is incorrect - Hero Fiennes-Tiffin played young Tom Riddle in Half-Blood Prince, not Chamber of Secrets. Christian Coulson played Tom Riddle in Chamber of Secrets.

passages.text: The casting of Hero Fiennes-Tiffin as the 11-year-old Tom Riddle in Half-Blood Prince was particularly notable because he is the son of Ralph Fiennes, creating a unique family connection between the young and adult versions of Voldemort in the film series.
passages.explanation: This is incorrect - Hero Fiennes-Tiffin is Ralph Fiennes' nephew, not his son.

passages.text: In Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, the orphanage scenes featuring young Tom Riddle were filmed with Hero Fiennes-Tiffin, whose performance demonstrated the early signs of the manipulative charm that would later define Voldemort's character throughout the series.
passages.explanation: This is correct - Hero Fiennes-Tiffin did appear in the orphanage scenes as young Tom Riddle in Half-Blood Prince.

passages.text: Frank Dillane's portrayal of teenage Tom Riddle in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince includes the pivotal scene where he manipulates Professor Slughorn into revealing information about Horcruxes, showcasing the character's growing darkness and cunning during his seventh year at Hogwarts.
passages.explanation: This is correct - Frank Dillane played teenage Tom Riddle in the Horcrux memory scene with Slughorn.

answer_to_question: Hero Fiennes-Tiffin plays the 11-year-old Tom Riddle (young Voldemort) in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, appearing in the orphanage memory scenes. Frank Dillane plays the teenage version of Tom Riddle in the same film, appearing in the Hogwarts memory sequences including the crucial scene with Professor Slughorn about Horcruxes.

passages.text: Dragon Ball GT chief character designer Katsuyoshi Nakatsuru said he agonized over designing Goku's Super Saiyan 4 appearance, which was the idea of the show's producers, questioning whether it was necessary to go further with the transformations. Because Super Saiyan 4 is brought about while in a Saiyan's Ōzaru (大猿, lit. "Great Ape") form, he made the hair more "wild" and covered Goku's body in red fur. There was only a single final draft of the character, although Nakatsuru did consider making the hair blonde, he ended up choosing black as it provides more contrast with the red fur.
passages.explanation: This passage is correct and describes the design process for Super Saiyan 4, explaining it requires the Great Ape form and features black hair with red fur.

passages.text: During the Shadow Dragon Saga in Dragon Ball GT, Goku first achieves Super Saiyan 4 when facing the One-Star Dragon, Omega Shenron. The transformation occurs after Goku regains his adult body and taps into his primal Saiyan instincts while maintaining his rational mind. This marked the first time in the series that a Saiyan had reached this legendary fourth level of Super Saiyan transformation.
passages.explanation: This passage is incorrect. Goku first achieved Super Saiyan 4 earlier in GT during the Baby Saga, not during the Shadow Dragon Saga against Omega Shenron.

passages.text: In Dragon Ball GT, Goku's transformation into Super Saiyan 4 represents a unique evolutionary path that differs from the traditional Super Saiyan transformations. Unlike Super Saiyan 1, 2, and 3 which amplify ki and change hair color, Super Saiyan 4 requires the Saiyan to first transform into their Great Ape form and then regain their human consciousness while maintaining the ape's primal power.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly explains that Super Saiyan 4 is different from other Super Saiyan forms and requires the Great Ape transformation followed by regaining human consciousness.

passages.text: Five years later, Goku meets his evil older brother Raditz and sacrifices himself to defeat Raditz after he learns about his heritage. Goku comes from a race of extraterrestrials called Saiyans, himself having been sent from their home planet to prepare Earth for sale on the intergalactic market by destroying all its life. While Grandpa Gohan was taking care of him, Goku suffered a severe head injury and forgets his mission to conquer Earth. During his epic battle with Frieza, Goku becomes the first Saiyan in a thousand years to transform into a fabled Super Saiyan.
passages.explanation: This passage is correct and describes Goku's background and his first Super Saiyan transformation during the battle with Frieza, making him the first Super Saiyan in a thousand years.

passages.text: The Super Saiyan 4 transformation first occurred during the Baby Saga of Dragon Ball GT when Goku was fighting Baby Vegeta. After being transformed back into a child by the Black Star Dragon Balls, Goku struggled to achieve higher Super Saiyan levels until Pan helped him regain his tail, allowing him to transform into a Golden Great Ape and subsequently achieve Super Saiyan 4.
passages.explanation: This passage is correct. Goku first achieved Super Saiyan 4 during the Baby Saga, and Pan did help him by allowing him to see the Earth, which helped him regain control and transform.

passages.text: Dragon Ball GT introduced the Super Saiyan 4 transformation as a form that bypasses the traditional Golden Great Ape stage entirely. Instead, Goku achieved this form through intense meditation and ki control training with the Supreme Kai, allowing him to access primal Saiyan power without the need for the Ōzaru transformation that had been established in earlier series.
passages.explanation: This passage is incorrect. Super Saiyan 4 does not bypass the Golden Great Ape stage - it actually requires it. Goku did not achieve it through training with the Supreme Kai but through the Golden Great Ape transformation.

passages.text: The timeline of Goku's Super Saiyan transformations spans multiple series, with his first Super Saiyan achieved during the Frieza Saga in Dragon Ball Z, followed by Super Saiyan 2 and 3 in later arcs. The Super Saiyan 4 transformation was introduced years later in Dragon Ball GT as the ultimate Saiyan form, representing a return to the race's more primitive and instinctual nature rather than the refined energy-based transformations of the previous forms.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly outlines the progression of Goku's Super Saiyan transformations across the different series and accurately describes Super Saiyan 4 as representing a more primitive, instinctual approach.

answer_to_question: Based on the passages, Goku first achieved the Super Saiyan 4 transformation during the Baby Saga of Dragon Ball GT when he was fighting Baby Vegeta. After being transformed back into a child by the Black Star Dragon Balls, Pan helped him regain his tail, which allowed him to transform into a Golden Great Ape and subsequently achieve Super Saiyan 4. This transformation required him to first enter the Great Ape (Ōzaru) form and then regain his human consciousness while maintaining the ape's primal power, representing a unique evolutionary path that differs from the traditional Super Saiyan transformations.

passages.text: Vanessa received an SMS which reveals that Dan was "Gossip Girl". Her cameo was filmed on the set of the Sex and The City prequel, The Carrie Diaries; the producers like to imagine that she was directing an episode.
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage and is factually correct about Vanessa's ending.

passages.text: In the series finale, Vanessa appears briefly in a flash-forward sequence showing her successful career as a documentary filmmaker, having moved permanently to Los Angeles to pursue her artistic ambitions.
passages.explanation: This is false - Vanessa's actual ending involved receiving the SMS about Dan being Gossip Girl and her cameo being filmed on The Carrie Diaries set, not a flash-forward showing her as a documentary filmmaker in LA.

passages.text: Vanessa's final scene in the series serves as a meta-reference to the show's production, as her cameo appearance was actually shot during the filming of The Carrie Diaries, another CW series set in the same universe.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes how Vanessa's final appearance was handled through the connection to The Carrie Diaries production.

passages.text: Vanessa received an email notification which reveals that Nate was "Gossip Girl". Her final appearance was filmed on the set of the Sex and The City sequel series; the producers like to imagine that she was producing an episode.
passages.explanation: This is false - it was Dan, not Nate, who was revealed as Gossip Girl, and it was an SMS not an email. Also, she was imagined to be directing, not producing.

passages.text: The character of Vanessa Abrams concludes her arc by learning the truth about the anonymous blogger's identity through a text message, connecting her storyline to the show's central mystery.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes how Vanessa learns about Dan being Gossip Girl through the SMS, linking her to the show's main plot revelation.

passages.text: Vanessa's character exits the main narrative in earlier seasons, but returns for the series finale where she reconciles with Dan and they begin dating again after he confesses to being Gossip Girl.
passages.explanation: This is false - Vanessa and Dan do not reconcile or begin dating again in the finale. She simply receives the SMS revelation about his identity.

passages.text: The writers incorporated Vanessa's final moment into the broader Gossip Girl universe by having her cameo filmed during production of The Carrie Diaries, suggesting her continued involvement in television production.
passages.explanation: This correctly describes how the writers handled Vanessa's ending by connecting it to The Carrie Diaries production and implying her career in television.

answer_to_question: At the end of Gossip Girl, Vanessa Abrams receives an SMS revealing that Dan was Gossip Girl. Her final cameo appearance was filmed on the set of The Carrie Diaries (the Sex and the City prequel), with the producers imagining that she was directing an episode. This creative choice served as both a meta-reference to the show's production and a way to suggest Vanessa's continued involvement in television, connecting her storyline to the show's central mystery revelation while incorporating her into the broader Gossip Girl universe.

passages.text: The series stars Freddie Highmore as Shaun Murphy, a young savant autistic surgical resident at San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital. Antonia Thomas, Nicholas Gonzalez, Beau Garrett, Hill Harper, Richard Schiff, and Tamlyn Tomita also star in the show. The series received a put pilot commitment at ABC after a previous attempted series did not move forward at CBS Television Studios in 2015; The Good Doctor was ordered to series in May 2017. On October 3, 2017, ABC picked up the series for a full season of 18 episodes. The series is primarily filmed in Vancouver, British Columbia. In March 2018, ABC renewed the series for a second season.
passages.explanation: This is the original seed passage that provides factual information about The Good Doctor series, including the renewal for a second season in March 2018.

passages.text: Following strong ratings performance in its sophomore year, The Good Doctor was renewed for a third season in February 2019. The series continued to maintain solid viewership numbers, leading ABC to greenlight a fourth season in April 2020. The show's consistent performance and critical acclaim helped secure its position in ABC's programming lineup for multiple consecutive seasons.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly describes the renewal pattern for seasons 3 and 4 of The Good Doctor.

passages.text: The Good Doctor reached a significant milestone when ABC announced the renewal for both fifth and sixth seasons simultaneously in May 2021. This dual-season pickup demonstrated the network's confidence in the medical drama's continued success. The sixth season, which premiered in October 2022, marked another chapter in Shaun Murphy's journey at San Jose St. Bonaventure Hospital.
passages.explanation: This passage accurately describes the dual renewal for seasons 5 and 6, which was a real occurrence for the series.

passages.text: In a surprising turn of events, ABC announced in January 2023 that The Good Doctor would conclude with its seventh season, making it the final chapter of Shaun Murphy's story. passages.text: In North American residential construction, aluminum wire was used for wiring entire houses for a short time from the 1960s to the mid-1970s during a period of high copper prices. Electrical devices (outlets, switches, lighting, fans, etc.) at the time were not designed with the particular properties of the aluminum wire being used in mind, and there were some issues related to the properties of the wire itself, making the installations with aluminum wire much more susceptible to problems. Revised manufacturing standards for both the wire and the devices were developed to reduce the problems. Existing homes with this older aluminum wiring used in branch circuits present a potential fire hazard.
passages.explanation: This is one of the original seed passages and is factually correct about aluminum wiring usage from the 1960s to mid-1970s.

passages.text: Ontario's Electrical Safety Authority documented that aluminum branch circuit wiring installations peaked between 1968 and 1976, with the majority of problematic installations occurring during this eight-year window. The province saw widespread adoption of aluminum wiring in suburban developments, particularly in the Greater Toronto Area and Ottawa regions, before safety concerns and revised building codes effectively ended its residential use by the late 1970s.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies the peak period of aluminum wiring use in Ontario and when it effectively ended.

passages.text: Canadian electrical codes were updated in the early 1980s to restrict the use of aluminum wiring in residential branch circuits, following documented fire incidents and safety studies. Ontario adopted these federal code changes, effectively prohibiting new aluminum branch circuit installations in homes built after 1982, though aluminum continued to be permitted for larger gauge applications like service entrance conductors.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly states that aluminum wiring was restricted in the early 1980s and prohibited after 1982, when in reality the phase-out occurred in the mid-to-late 1970s due to safety concerns and market forces, not code changes in the 1980s.

passages.text: The Ontario Ministry of Consumer and Commercial Relations issued guidelines in 1977 recommending against the use of aluminum wiring in new residential construction, citing fire safety concerns and connection reliability issues. Most builders in Ontario had already transitioned back to copper wiring by this time due to stabilizing copper prices and growing awareness of aluminum wiring problems.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies the timeframe when Ontario authorities recommended against aluminum wiring use and when builders had largely transitioned back to copper.

passages.text: In Ontario, aluminum wiring continued to be widely used in residential construction through the early 1980s, with many homes built between 1975 and 1983 containing aluminum branch circuits. The transition away from aluminum occurred gradually as copper prices decreased and electrical contractors became more familiar with proper aluminum installation techniques, leading to its eventual discontinuation by the mid-1980s.
passages.explanation: This passage incorrectly extends the timeline of aluminum wiring use into the early-to-mid 1980s, when in reality its use had largely ended by the mid-1970s in Ontario residential construction.

passages.text: By 1976, most major home builders in Ontario had voluntarily ceased using aluminum wiring for branch circuits due to mounting insurance concerns and liability issues. The combination of documented electrical fires, difficult insurance coverage, and returning copper price stability made aluminum wiring economically unviable for residential applications, leading to its rapid abandonment in the province.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies 1976 as when most Ontario builders stopped using aluminum wiring and accurately describes the economic and safety factors that drove this decision.

passages.text: The Canadian Standards Association revised its electrical installation standards in 1975 to address aluminum wiring safety concerns, leading Ontario to implement stricter inspection requirements for homes using aluminum branch circuits. These enhanced safety measures, while improving installation quality, ultimately contributed to builders' decision to return to copper wiring by 1976-1977 due to increased compliance costs.
passages.explanation: This passage correctly identifies the mid-1970s timeframe for standards revisions and the subsequent return to copper wiring in Ontario due to both safety and economic factors.

answer_to_question: Based on the passages, aluminum wiring stopped being used in Ontario residential construction in the mid-to-late 1970s, specifically around 1976-1977. The phase-out began in the mid-1970s due to safety concerns, fire hazards, insurance issues, and stabilizing copper prices, with most major builders voluntarily ceasing its use by 1976 and official recommendations against its use issued in 1977.

passages.text: The 2018 Winter Olympics, officially known as the XXIII Olympic Winter Games (French: Les XXIIIèmes Jeux olympiques d'hiver; Hangul: 제23회 동계 올림픽; RR: Je-isipsamhoe Donggye Ollimpik) and commonly known as PyeongChang 2018 ([pʰjʌŋ.tɕʰaŋ]), is a major international multi-sport event scheduled to take place from 9 to 25 February 2018 in Pyeongchang County, South Korea.
